venue.name: Miracle Beach Nature House
venue.description: The Miracle Beach Nature House sits in Miracle Beach Park at Black Creek, on the coast midway between Courtenay and Campbell River, and is run by Discover Parks, a project of the BC Parks Foundation. It started in 1959 as a single tent staffed by one naturalist, the second of its kind in a BC park, and is now a permanent building across from the park amphitheatre. Inside are bones, interactive digital displays, painted ceiling murals and a small shop with frozen treats. Entry and taking part in the activities there are free, and the building opens for the summer season only.

facility_notes.washrooms: The Miracle Beach Nature House can be reached from the day-use area parking lot. There is parking and washrooms available.
facility_notes.lunch_space: The park's own facility list includes picnic areas and picnic shelters, and there is a large picnic area overlooking the water. Nothing says whether a group may eat inside the Nature House.

restrictions: In your exploration, please remember to carefully place overturned rocks in their original position. Look but do not touch or remove any shells or marine organisms from the park.
During the winter, horses are only allowed on the road between the gatehouse and group site. Horses are not permitted on any other trails within the park.
venue.hours_notes: In the summer season the Nature House is open daily in July and August, Sunday to Thursday 9:30 to 4:30, Friday 9:30 to 5:30 and Saturday 9:30 to 6:30. BC Parks says it opens every weekend from the May long weekend and then daily from late June through Labour Day.
venue.seasonal_notes: Discover Parks now lists the Miracle Beach Nature House as closed, with a line saying see you in Summer 2027. Until it reopens, anything you plan here has to happen outdoors in the park. The park itself is very busy through the summer.
venue.price_year_or_season: The opening hours on their activity page still finish with a last day of the season of September 1st, 2025, so that timetable is from an earlier summer than the one just gone.

programs.name: Visit to the Nature House
programs.description: A free, self guided visit to the Nature House building, reached from the day-use area parking lot and sitting right across from the park amphitheatre. Discover Parks describes bones, interactive digital displays, ceiling murals and a small shop with frozen treats, and says friendly Park Ambassadors are there to answer questions about the park's plants and animals. They rate it easy, list no maximum group size and allow dogs on a leash. The building is the hub for Jerry's Rangers, guest speakers and free kids' movie nights in the summer. It was listed as closed for the season when we checked, with a note about reopening in summer 2027.
programs.what_children_do: Go inside the one room building and look at the bones and the display cases, try the interactive digital displays and the Mystery Box, and look up at the orcas painted across the ceiling.
programs.our_note: It is one room, so half an hour is closer to the mark than a morning. Check it is actually open before you set out, because their own page says it is shut until summer 2027 and there is no phone number or email published for the building. Pair it with the interpretive loop that starts just outside so the trip is worth the drive.
programs.practical_summary: You reach it from the day-use car park, where there is parking and there are washrooms. The park has picnic areas and picnic shelters for lunch. Nothing says whether a bus can park or whether the building is step free, so ask.
programs.evidence: The Miracle Beach Nature House is a great place to learn about the park’s amazing plants and animals from our friendly Park Ambassadors.

programs.name: Nature House Interpretive Loop audio tour
programs.description: A free self guided walk around the Nature House Interpretive Loop with recorded commentary, narrated by Emma, a long time member of the Miracle Beach Nature House staff. The loop is 0.64 km with 14 m of elevation gain, rated easy, and goes through the forest with stops about plants and the history of the park. A PDF guide with extra visuals goes with the audio. The walk starts to the left of the Nature House, past the large carved sculpture, where a poster on the wall carries a QR code. The commentary is in English. You have to log in to Discover Parks to play the full track or open the guide, and cell reception in the park can be poor for some providers, so download it before you arrive. Discover Parks lists it year round, but says availability follows the park's seasonal operation and the weather.
programs.what_children_do: Walk a short forest loop, stopping where the recording tells them to, looking at the trees and plants it names along the way.
programs.our_note: The audio and the printable guide both sit behind a log in on their site, so set that up at the office rather than in the car park. Download it before you leave town too, because the signal in the park is patchy. At 0.64 km the loop is short enough for small legs.
programs.practical_summary: The walk starts beside the Nature House, which is reached from the day-use car park where there is parking and there are washrooms. It is outdoors the whole way on a forest trail, and no cover is mentioned if it rains.
programs.evidence: This 0.64km loop hike takes you through the forest with stops to learn about plants and the unique history of the park.

programs.name: Summer drop-in programs at the amphitheatre
programs.description: Through the summer, Jerry's Rangers activities, special guest speakers, trivia nights and movie nights are held regularly in the amphitheatre near the Nature House. Discover Parks says entry to the Nature House and taking part in all activities is free, and points to the Miracle Beach Park page for upcoming events and to the Nature House's Instagram account for programme schedules and up to date hours. No dates, start times, ages, group sizes or booking route are published for any of these, and the individual pages for Jerry's Rangers here, for the arts and crafts sessions at the Nature House and for the Friday trivia nights are not live on their site.
programs.our_note: These are drop in rather than booked, and nothing on their site says when any of them run, so they are not something to build a trip around. The only schedule they point you to is the Nature House's own Instagram account. Worth a look again next spring, once the building reopens.
programs.practical_summary: It all happens outdoors at the amphitheatre near the Nature House, in the summer season only. Washrooms and parking are at the day-use area, and the park has picnic areas and shelters.
programs.evidence: Entry to the Nature House and participation in all activities is free, however donations are always appreciated!

images.alt: The inside of a wooden building with a mural of orcas swimming painted across the sloped ceiling, two large cartoon moose painted on the plank wall, glass cases of stuffed animals and bones along the left side, and a white cabinet labelled The Mystery Box.
